sovereign_country.strategic_role: 苏伊士运河经济特区、辐射中东及北非的低成本轻工制造

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Bulk Transactional Email API and Newsletter Hosting Platform

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic-based codes with Islamic Sharia as a primary source of legislation)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt–United Arab Emirates Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended by Law No. 180 of 2018) and its Implementing Regulations, Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (as amended), Executive Regulations of Law No. 80 of 2002 (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 95 of 2016), Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT directives, and the Financial Regulatory Authority decisions on beneficial ownership registers.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum of Association and Draft Articles of Association
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholders assembled in Egypt; notarized at the Egyptian Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if copies are used abroad; otherwise standard Egyptian notarization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney for Incorporation Agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization at the Egyptian Embassy/Consulate in the country of origin, or Hague Apostille (Apostille Convention in force for Egypt since May 15, 2022)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of Passport and Corporate Registry Extract for Corporate Shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Passport Issuing Authority and Foreign Company Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the foreign competent authority, followed by certified Arabic translation and Egyptian legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) watchlists, OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, EU restrictive measures, and Central Bank of Egypt blacklists. Politically exposed persons (PEPs) are subject to enhanced due diligence including senior management approval, source of wealth verification, and ongoing transaction monitoring in accordance with Law No. 80 of 2002 and FATF recommendations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Investor Portal (GAFI One-Stop Shop) and the Egyptian Commercial Registry electronic name reservation system
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All statutory company names must be registered in Arabic. A non-Arabic/transliterated name is displayed on the commercial registration card and in trade invoices, but the Arabic name governs official correspondence. Transliteration must follow Egyptian Ministry of Trade and Industry orthography standards and avoid misleading Latin-script variants.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms that falsely imply government, state, or sovereign sponsorship: 'Egyptian', 'National', 'Central', 'Republic', 'Government', 'President'
Terms that imply an already-regulated financial activity without a license: 'Bank', 'Finance', 'Insurance', 'Exchange', 'Securities'
Terms that require special ministerial approval: 'University', 'Academy', 'Military', 'Nuclear'
Names of foreign states, international organizations, or recognizable political entities
Misleading terms about the company object or terms contrary to public policy
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name is rejected, the applicant may file a written appeal to the GAFI Appeal Committee within 60 days of the rejection notice, stating the legal and factual rebuttal. The Committee must issue a decision within 15 working days. If the rejection is upheld, the same name cannot be refiled, but a modified name may be submitted. An adverse decision may be finally challenged before the Egyptian Administrative Court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or letterbox address is not generally acceptable for a newly incorporated Egyptian LLC. The company must have a physical registered office in Egypt evidenced by a lease agreement or ownership title and a commercial license for use of the premises. Email-infrastructure and newsletter-hosting companies are subject to the same physical presence requirement and cannot rely on a purely virtual address for AML/CFT place-of-management purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate to elevated — GAFI, Commercial Registry, and the Tax Authority perform unannounced inspections, particularly within the first operational year. The likelihood of a physical inspection is estimated at 15–25%, increasing if the registered address is a shared sub-lease, a P.O. Box, or a location inconsistent with the declared business activity.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under GAFI fee schedule (approx. EGP 300–500)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: One-stop-shop LLC incorporation and registration fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for standard LLC registration without minimum capital requirement (approx. EGP 13,000–15,000 equivalent)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial tariff for corporate documents of approximately 30 pages plus stamp duties

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial Registry initial certificate and extract fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial Registry under Ministry of Trade and Industry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration certificate and extract tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication expenses in the Official Gazette
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Legal advertisement tariff calculated on line count and page format

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization of foreign corporate shareholders' documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and competent foreign apostille authorities
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document fees (apostille USD 50–80 per document; Egyptian consular legalization per signature)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Arabic translation of foreign corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Egyptian translator / Ministry of Justice certified translation office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of approximately USD 8–12 per page for a 10-page set

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 4 of 2025 (new Egyptian Companies Law, effective 2025) — general incorporation and limited liability company chapters, together with the Executive Regulations issued thereunder; transitional interpretive principles of Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and Executive Regulation Decree No. 96 of 1982
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Companies Registration One-Stop-Shop; Commercial Registry Department, Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association (Aqd al-Ta'sis) and Articles of Association (Nizam al-Asasi) executed before the Ministry of Justice Notary Public and filed electronically via the GAFI unified e-registration portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for LLCs under Law No. 4 of 2025; the founders may declare a nominal share capital, and any declared capital must be fully paid in and deposited into a temporary escrowed account at an Egyptian bank before registration, with release or return upon issuance of the commercial registration certificate
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: This First Board Resolution of [EG_LLC], adopted on the ____ day of ________, 20____ at the registered office, is passed under Law No. 4 of 2025: (1) Ratification: the incorporation formalities completed with GAFI are hereby ratified; (2) Share Subscription: the nominal share capital of EGP ______ is confirmed fully subscribed and paid up; (3) Registered Office: [full Cairo address] is adopted as the statutory seat for all official service; (4) Officers: [Founder A] is appointed First Manager and sole authorized bank signatory, and [Founder B] is appointed Deputy Manager and second signatory; (5) Banking: [Bank name] is approved as the principal bank; (6) Delegation: management is authorized to obtain the tax card, register with NISA, and secure the office facility and civil defense clearances.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI unified electronic window (www.established.gov.eg / GAFI One-Stop-Shop, Cairo)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three proposed Arabic and English company names through the GAFI portal; pay the reservation fee; obtain electronic pre-approval; the name must not duplicate existing commercial registry entries (Ramooz) or registered trademarks.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID copies of all founding members
Power of attorney in favor of the registered filer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any name is rejected, resubmit with alternative names; no fee refund is processed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice Notary Public Office in the notary district of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association before the notary; verify the identities of all founders; pay stamp and notarization fees; e-notarization by digital signature is accepted under the 2025 electronic incorporation regime.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
ID or passport copies of founders
Lease or title deed of registered office address with owner consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct signature or date anomalies and re-execute; provide a valid power of attorney if a representative signs for a corporate founder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Registration and Commercial Registry Entry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Registration Department / Commercial Registry (Ramooz) at the One-Stop-Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation application electronically attaching the notarized Memorandum and Articles; pay registration and commercial register fees; receive the company registry number and commercial registration extract (Akhraj Ramooz); the LLC attains legal personality upon issuance.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Bank capital deposit certificate (if declared capital is paid)
Notarized office lease with building safety documentation
ID or passport copies of founders and appointed managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond within the statutory 30-day period to GAFI queries; amend the constitutive documents or file supplementary declarations; resubmit corrected data through the e-registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Tax Card Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — designated Taxpayer Center based on assessed size
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the LLC with ETA; obtain the tax card (Bitaka Darbiya) and tax identification number; enroll for corporate income tax, stamp duty, VAT, and payroll withholding; activate the e-invoicing regime and file the required data through the ETA e-platform.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Manager ID or passport and specimen signature
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify mismatches between registry, lease, and ID data; file an administrative correction request if the tax card address or ISIC activity code is misclassified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NISA) regional office / e-portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the establishment registration form (Form 1) and employee declaration (Form 2); register the LLC as an employer; obtain the insurance registration number for the entity and each employee; set up monthly contribution statements.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File supplementary correction forms for missing prior employment records; pay minimal acceptable contributions under the NISA installment scheme.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Facility Operating Certificate and Civil Defense Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Municipality (Hayy) licensing office; Civil Defense Directorate, Ministry of Interior
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for a facility operating certificate (Izhār) for office premises; undergo civil defense inspection covering fire safety, egress routes, suppression equipment, and emergency signage; obtain the Izhār that serves as the physical premises business license.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Remediate fire safety deficiencies, install additional suppression equipment and signage, and re-inspect; escalate to the district management level if the clearance is delayed beyond SLA.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — commercial and trade registry; Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT) policy guidelines for ICT services; National Telecom Regulatory Authority (NTRA) for OTT classification
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No ICT operating license required — email newsletter and transactional email platform qualifies as an exempted over-the-top (OTT) content application under NTRA practice; the office facility is cleared via the Izhār municipal operating certificate

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C (Green List) — environmental registration only; no full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Report required for office or data-hosting premises with no industrial discharge
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Law No. 4/1994 on Environment (as amended by Law No. 202/2020): no process wastewater discharge; rainwater drainage per Governorate Decree standards; standby generator exhaust limited to ambient air quality thresholds set by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 964/2015; defective IT hardware and e-waste transferred only to EEAA-licensed handlers per Decree No. 710/2022

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Directorate fire-safety certificate covering extinguishers, emergency exits, alarm systems, and smoke detectors; structural load clearance for server and equipment racks; occupational safety notification under Labor Law No. 12/2003 and health registration where the employee headcount exceeds the statutory threshold

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) of the Ministry of Finance; unified Tax Identification Number (TIN) issuance via the ETA electronic tax portal (eta.gov.eg) and the e-invoicing system (einvoice.gov.eg)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned LLC must apply through the ETA electronic registration portal within 30 days of commencing business or establishing a permanent establishment, submitting the notarized and Arabic-legalized incorporation deed, power of attorney to the registered tax agent, signed lease or address certificate, passport copies of managers and directors, and a bank account confirmation (minimum capital is not statutorily mandated); the ETA issues a single unified TIN covering income tax, VAT, and stamp duty within approximately 15-30 working days of complete filing; non-resident software and email-infrastructure suppliers without a PE must register for VAT only if they make taxable supplies deemed situated in Egypt (notably B2C electronic and digital services), and the ETA may require designation of an Egyptian resident tax representative
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt provides no check-the-box or pass-through election for LLCs; the available elective mechanisms are: (i) cash-basis accounting for small taxpayers whose annual turnover does not exceed EGP 10 million, (ii) consolidated corporate tax group filing for a resident parent holding at least 95% of subsidiaries, (iii) the VAT credit refund or offset election for exporters, and (iv) group VAT registration; hybrid mismatch outcomes are neutralized by mandatory disallowance rules enacted under BEPS Action 2 via law amendments effective 2023, without elective relief

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax) regime under Law No. 67/2016 and its Executive Bylaw
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual value of taxable supplies for mandatory VAT registration, with voluntary registration permitted from EGP 50,000; non-resident suppliers of electronic and digital services are registrable without local turnover threshold when the place of supply is deemed to be Egypt and the recipient is a non-registered private person or an Egyptian taxable person
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory national e-Invoice and e-Receipt regime with real-time fiscal clearance through the ETA Central Data Center (CDC); registered taxpayers are onboarded in phases by turnover band and must transmit invoice JSON/XML files via approved APIs (or the ETA portal for micro-taxpayers), receive a Unique Identification Code (UUID), and embed a QR code or digital stamp before the invoice becomes legally valid; B2B invoices submitted for a given day are cleared on a near-real-time basis, rejected files attract automatic suspension of VAT account privileges, and e-receipt obligations apply to B2C supplies in the retail and service sectors

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT rate applies to exports of goods and services under Law No. 67/2016 when the customer is a non-resident, consideration is received in foreign currency, and the service (including email newsletter infrastructure, transactional email APIs, and hosting platforms) is effectively used or consumed outside Egypt; the exporter must hold a written export contract or subscription agreement, service delivery evidence, and a bank documentary credit or remittance record; input VAT on purchases attributable to such exports is creditable and refundable through the ETA VAT refund mechanism subject to a desk audit
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration in the Single Administrative Document format, processed electronically through the NAFIZA national single window and stamped by the Egyptian Customs Authority
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or equivalent Certificate of Non-Physical Delivery evidencing transfer of title or offshore provision of the digital and email-infrastructure service
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by a licensed Egyptian bank documenting receipt of the foreign-currency export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rated export claims are subject to ETA ex-post documentary audits and desk reviews of the full proof bundle; if export status is not substantiated, the tax authority claws back the VAT credit with a 2% per month late-payment charge, imposes an additional penalty of up to 40% of the tax evaded, and, upon a finding of forged export documentation, false remittance certificates, or sham non-resident contracts, refers the case to criminal prosecution carrying imprisonment of up to five years and joint personal liability of signatories under the Unified Tax Procedures Law No. 206/2020 and Law No. 67/2016

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) under Law No. 194 of 2020 (Central Bank and Banking System Law), acting as the exclusive monetary authority, foreign-exchange regulator and banking supervisor; CBE-licensed banks are the only authorized dealers permitted to execute currency transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Since the March 2024 exchange-rate reform, the CBE operates a flexible, market-determined regime and has dismantled the administrative FX rationing of 2022-2023. Current-account items, including cross-border SaaS licence fees, email-infrastructure hosting and software services, are convertible through authorized dealers upon presentation of a signed contract, commercial invoice and valid tax documentation. Capital-account transactions of GAFI-registered foreign investors are protected under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, but profit remittance and capital repatriation require audited financial statements, proof of settlement of all corporate and withholding taxes, a GAFI registration certificate, and a bank remittance application; post-reform the primary practical hurdle is the bank's sequential documentary review rather than scarcity of FX. Unofficial parallel-market conversion and non-bank foreign-exchange intermediation remain criminal offences under Egyptian law.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters of software and technology services must repatriate 100% of invoice proceeds to an Egyptian bank account through an authorized dealer within 6 months of the invoice or shipment date, extendable to a maximum of 12 months only with CBE-approved justification. Under the post-March-2024 flexible-rate regime, no fixed statutory percentage of export proceeds must be mandatorily converted into EGP; proceeds may be retained in a foreign-currency account of the exporter. However, the bank issues the official export-proceeds certificate only after verifying the underlying service agreement, commercial invoice, collection evidence and settlement record, and that certificate is a precondition for claiming VAT input credits and for corporate tax treatment of the export revenue.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational EGP Account and USD/EUR Foreign-Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account (pre-incorporation share-capital subscription) and Operational EGP Account
Operational EGP Account and USD Foreign-Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium (restricted). Egypt does not offer an EMI licence class equivalent to the EU or UK regime. Payment services, e-money issuance and digital banking activities require a CBE or Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) licence under Payment Systems Law No. 18 of 2019 and CBE fintech rules. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise Business, Airwallex, Payoneer) cannot clear EGP, open regulated onshore accounts for the EG LLC, or serve as the primary clearing rail. They remain viable only as ancillary collection or payout interfaces for the offshore parent receiving Stripe and card-not-present proceeds in USD/EUR; all onshore liquidity must flow through a CBE-licensed bank and its correspondent network.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory as a general rule. Under CBE AML/CFT directives implementing AML Law No. 8 of 2002, the EG LLC's authorized signatories, at least one director with signing authority, and each UBO holding 25% or more of the equity must appear before the bank's compliance officer with original identification documents. A foreign-resident director may be represented through a notarized power of attorney legalized at the competent Egyptian consulate and translated into Arabic, but the natural person presenting the POA must still appear physically for the interview. Remote end-to-end corporate onboarding is not available for foreign-controlled entities and does not waive the face-to-face meeting requirement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO structure involving non-Egyptian high-risk or offshore jurisdictions inconsistent with the declared Egyptian IT/SaaS business activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified register extracts and GAFI investment certificate; apostilled or consular-legalized certificates of incorporation for each parent layer; passports and proof of residential address for all UBOs; full ownership-chain organogram; source-of-wealth documentation comprising bank statements and audited financial statements; and a board statement explaining the commercial rationale for establishing the Egyptian entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intangible-service exporter flagged for high incoming wire volumes without physically verifiable goods flow (email API and newsletter SaaS revenue).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master service agreements with named customers; sample commercial invoices; six consecutive months of Stripe settlement statements; domain-ownership verification and platform technical description; ISIC 6201 / NAICS 518210 registration excerpt; PCI-DSS attestation; and a reconciled revenue pipeline demonstrating recurring subscription billing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Turnover forecast disproportionately high relative to the EG LLC's stated paid-in capital, creating money-laundering or round-tripping concern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved business plan and revenue model; audited or reviewed management accounts; banker's reference from the parent company's bank; capital-injection inward remittance certificate; and a funds-flow policy segregating capital, operating collections and distributable reserves, with 85-90% of collections onward-disbursed to verified suppliers or held in regulated deposits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aggregated small-ticket card payouts from Stripe Billing flagged as possible card-not-present laundering or money-muling.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Stripe merchant agreement and account verification letter; subscription-billing logic and refund-policy documentation; chargeback history report; PCI-DSS compliance certificate; transaction-level reconciliation report; and the company's written AML/CFT procedures designating a compliance officer responsible for ongoing monitoring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid commingling of capital injection, operating revenue and dividend remittance within the first twelve months of operation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Account-purpose memorandum; designated foreign-currency capital account subject to CBE investment registration; inward remittance certificate; first-year cash-flow budget; board-approved allocation policy separating capital, operating and reserve funds; and audited financial statements evidencing distributable profits for any dividend payment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign shareholder must route funds by SWIFT MT103 from a licensed banking institution to the EG LLC's CBE-licensed account, instructing the CBE trade-nature code for direct investment/equity subscription and stating the purpose as 'Investment in share capital of EG LLC'. The receiving bank verifies the certificate of incorporation, GAFI commercial-registry excerpt, current UBO register and a board resolution approving the capital subscription. USD amounts are credited to the designated foreign-currency account, after which the bank issues an inward remittance certificate and files a transaction report for any remittance exceeding the CBE reporting threshold; the funds may then be converted to EGP at the prevailing market rate or retained in USD for onward cross-border disbursement. All wire instructions must state the precise ISIC/NAICS business activity to avoid misclassification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The EG LLC's outbound settlement rail is SWIFT MT103 for service payments (cloud-hosting fees, software licences, contractor wages) using CBE purpose codes for 'fees for services rendered' and 'royalties and software licences'; each transfer requires an underlying invoice or contract retained in the bank's electronic document window. Irrevocable commercial letters of credit are relevant only for physical imports such as server hardware and must be opened through the same CBE-licensed bank. Dividend and profit remittances to shareholders require audited accounts, proof of final withholding tax, a tax clearance certificate and a formal remittance application before execution of the MT103; the bank will verify GAFI foreign-investment registration at the point of remittance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward (USD/EGP or EUR/EGP) via a CBE-licensed dealer, supported by documented export invoices or import contracts; tenor limited to the underlying trade maturity, commonly up to 12 months; initial margin or collateral required; uncovered speculative positions prohibited.
FX swap (spot-to-forward) bridging EGP operational liquidity to USD disbursements, documented by invoice-level cash-flow schedules and subject to CBE position limits.

Cross-currency swap (USD/EGP) hedging a USD-denominated shareholder loan or term deposit, executed under an ISDA master agreement with an authorized dealer and approved by the CBE as a non-speculative derivative.

USD/EGP non-deliverable forward (NDF): not bookable by the onshore EG LLC; the CBE regime requires deliverable EGP settlement through an authorized dealer. Only the offshore parent or a dedicated group treasury vehicle may execute an NDF as a portfolio hedge, and it must never be intermediated through the Egyptian operating entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (CIT) with audited financial statements, transfer-pricing declaration, and related-party schedule attached
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Income Tax Sector
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after fiscal year-end; April 30 for a calendar-year LLC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 1% per month or fraction on unpaid tax; fixed late-filing fines of EGP 500 to EGP 5,000; enforced collection through bank attachment and receivables seizure; failure to file for two consecutive years enables GAFI administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual partners' general assembly resolution approving audited financial statements and profit appropriation, with minutes entered in the Minute Book and approved financial statements deposited with the corporate registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year-end; June 30 for a calendar-year LLC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monetary fines for late nondeposit; unlawful distributions are voidable and managers become jointly and severally liable; repeated failure to convene the annual assembly subjects the LLC to GAFI-ordered dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of the Commercial Registry certificate and commercial registration extract
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: During the month of January each calendar year; deadline January 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-renewal surcharge accrues immediately after January 31; the enterprise loses legal standing to execute contracts and may be suspended in the registry; sustained nonrenewal results in deletion and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal or validation of the taxpayer tax card and the economic activity certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) and the competent local business license authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in the January renewal window, aligned with commercial-registry renewal; no later than January 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines and blocking of e-invoicing registration, customs privileges, banking operations, and government tenders; prolonged nonrenewal triggers enforced tax registration and collection measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) confirmation return and updated beneficial-ownership register schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the commercial-registry renewal, joint submission by January 31; interim updates due within 30 days of any shareholding or control change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of EGP 20,000 to EGP 200,000 under AML Law 80/2002 as amended and Companies Law 4/2024; false or omitted UBO declarations invalidate share transfers and expose directors to disqualification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual payroll withholding tax reconciliation and cumulative employee salary income statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Salary and Income Tax Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before February 28 following the calendar year of wage payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unremitted withholding is treated as unpaid tax carrying 1% monthly additional tax; nonsubmission of the annual reconciliation attracts fixed penalties and blocks the tax clearance certificate required for commercial-registry renewal.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual social insurance wage declaration and contribution reconciliation (NSSA annual return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual wage-list declaration filed in the January–February cycle following each contribution year; deadline February 28
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines and interest under Social Insurance Law 148 of 2019; suspension of the employer insurance certificate and denial of tax clearance until the declaration is filed.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Companies Law No. 4 of 2024, every Egyptian LLC must appoint a certified external auditor approved by the partners' general assembly. A full statutory audit of the annual financial statements is compulsory where (i) issued capital exceeds EGP 2,000,000 (approximately USD 41,000), (ii) annual turnover exceeds EGP 20,000,000 (approximately USD 410,000), (iii) the LLC is controlled by or consolidates with a foreign parent, or (iv) the ETA requires audited accounts because the taxpayer carries related-party cross-border transactions. Smaller LLCs may discharge the requirement with a licensed-accountant review report for the annual assembly.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), substantially converged with IFRS; full IFRS as issued by the IASB is accepted for group consolidation and foreign-invested entities. Annual accounts must be presented in Egyptian Pounds and approved by the partners' general assembly.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LLC must maintain a beneficial-ownership register at its registered office identifying natural persons who ultimately own or control the LLC, including through foreign intermediate entities, per the ownership and control thresholds in Egypt's AML implementing regulations. The register is reviewed by the company secretary before each annual assembly; any share transfer or control change must be recorded and notified to GAFI within 30 days. An annual UBO confirmation is submitted jointly with the January commercial-registry renewal, and the approved register schedule is appended to the minutes of the annual partners' assembly. Deliberate concealment triggers AML penalties and suspension of transfer registration.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Managers (Directors) and their shareholdings
Minute Book of Partners' General Assemblies
Commercial Registry Extract and Tax Card copies

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% (Article 8, Law 91 of 2005, as amended; applied to net taxable income of an Egyptian LLC engaged in ISIC 6201)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No automatic statutory tax holiday for ISIC 6201. Investment Law 72/2017 offers a 50% tax reduction on income from core activities for newly established qualifying projects for up to 5 years, subject to ETA/Authority approval. Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) licensed projects may qualify for 0% corporate income tax for 5 years followed by a 50% reduction for 5 years. Exports of software services may benefit from promotional treatment, but approval-based; otherwise, standard rate applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 19 (Corporate Income Tax Return) under Law 91/2005; mandatory electronic filing via the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) portal at https://taxes.gov.eg; Transfer Pricing Declaration Form No. 59 must be attached when related-party transactions exist.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 4 months following the close of the fiscal year (Article 33, Law 91/2005); the fiscal year is typically the calendar year for Egyptian LLCs unless a different financial year has been approved by the ETA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate revenues from email API usage, newsletter hosting subscriptions, and infrastructure services, expressed in EGP using ETA-approved exchange rates for foreign currency receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the Egyptian LLC's worldwide income, including revenue received from the foreign parent through Stripe and credit card rails; e-invoice and e-receipt books must reconcile with the declared amount.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cloud infrastructure, SMTP delivery partner fees, data center, bandwidth, and direct hosting costs attributable to email sending services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are allowed only when supported by electronic tax invoices and arm's length evidence; any intercompany platform fees must be covered by Transfer Pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Employee salaries, rent, marketing, software subscriptions, depreciation, and general administrative expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany management fees, royalties, or marketing contributions to the non-resident parent are deductible only with a formal contract, withholding satisfaction, and TP benchmarking.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of aggregate related-party transactions with affiliates, including goods, services, intangibles, and financing; requires filing Transfer Pricing Declaration Form No. 59.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When aggregate related-party transactions exceed EGP 10 million for goods or EGP 5 million for services/financing/intangibles, a Local File must be prepared and available at the filing deadline even if not uploaded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit after statutory loss carryforwards multiplied by 22.5%; final settlement via the ETA nationwide collection system.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Prior quarterly advance payments are credited; any balance must be paid by the filing due date; proof of settlement is embedded in the e-filing workflow.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: procedural fine of EGP 5,000 to EGP 50,000 under Article 133 of Law 91/2005 as determined by the tax committee. Late payment: 2% monthly delay surcharge on the unpaid tax, capped at 50% of the tax due (Article 111). Understatement: additional tax plus a 50% penalty of the understated amount (Article 112). Failure to file beyond 150 days of the statutory deadline authorizes the ETA to assess a deemed tax ex parte; the e-filing portal also blocks subsequent transactions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory dividend withholding tax on profit distributions from an Egyptian LLC to its shareholders (Article 56, Law 91/2005); the withholding is a final tax for non-resident shareholders and is remitted by the LLC at the time of distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident shareholder must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) in its country of residence. The Egyptian LLC submits to the ETA the TRC, the relevant DTA article analysis, and a treaty-relief application prior to remittance. ETA reviews beneficial ownership and issues a reduced-rate confirmation. Under the Egypt-US treaty, dividends are reduced to 5% for corporate shareholders holding at least 10% capital and to 15% otherwise; other Egyptian DTAs generally provide 10%-15% dividend rates. Any payment made without prior approval exposes the LLC to the full 10% withholding and penalties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rates: 20% on royalties and 20% on interest paid to non-residents (Law 91/2005, Article 56). Treaty rates commonly reduce royalties to 10-15% (Egypt-US: 10%; Egypt-UK: 12%) and interest to 10-15% (Egypt-US: 15%). Reduced treaty rates require a valid TRC, a beneficial ownership declaration, and ETA approval before payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under Ministerial Decree 527/2020 and Article 37-bis of Law 91/2005: Master File is mandatory when the multinational group's consolidated annual revenue equals or exceeds EGP 5 billion. Local File is mandatory when aggregate related-party transactions reach EGP 10 million for tangible goods or EGP 5 million for services, intangibles, or financing in the tax year. Transfer Pricing Declaration Form No. 59 must be filed whenever related-party transactions exist, even below these thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations in the Caribbean format. Substance is enforced through the Egyptian GAAR (Article 30, Law 91/2005), beneficial ownership clauses in Egyptian DTAs, the MLI treaty-abuse rules, and ETA administrative practice. An Egyptian LLC lacking employees, premises, bank accounts, or genuine decision-making in Egypt is treated as a non-tax-resident shell or conduit; deductions are disallowed, treaty benefits denied, and profits re-characterized at the Egyptian-source level.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion - False Declaration or Concealed Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration of email API subscription revenue, omission of Stripe-funded foreign receipts from the Egyptian corporate return, fabrication of cloud infrastructure invoices to inflate deductible costs, or routing income through unregistered personal accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of 100%-300% of the evaded tax (Articles 134-135, Law 91/2005); civil assessment of the hidden tax plus a 50% delict penalty under Article 112; ex parte estimated assessment by the ETA using indirect liquidity methods when records are missing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and authorized signatories are jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax unless non-culpability is proven; travel bans on personal passports and bank asset freezes are imposed under tax collection enforcement; conviction triggers imprisonment and restitution orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the email newsletter infrastructure through an Egyptian LLC with zero employees, no office, and no local substance while all value creation and control remain abroad, using the entity solely to route invoices, commissions, or intercompany fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA disallowance of intra-group deductions, re-characterization of office income as Egyptian-source, application of the GAAR under Article 30, and reassessment at 22.5% without treaty shelter; 2% monthly delay surcharges capped at 50% plus procedural fines of up to EGP 50,000; potential VAT reassessment on undeclared service transfers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal civil restitution for intercompany expenses approved without arm's length evidence; travel bans and asset seizure; criminal exposure for aiding tax evasion of the foreign parent if the directors knowingly executed the conduit arrangement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Repatriating software subscription profits outside official banking channels, using hawala or unlicensed crypto exchanges, accepting settlement from sanctioned jurisdictions, or structuring split payments to evade the ETA collection system.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under AML Law 80/2002: imprisonment of up to 10 years and/or a fine of EGP 100,000 to EGP 1,000,000; confiscation of assets; listing and freeze orders by the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit; parallel USD-denominated OFAC sanctions exposure because the payment rails include Stripe and credit cards.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Direct criminal liability for executing or approving such transfers; personal confiscation of funds moved to personal accounts; permanent travel ban; arrest warrant; disqualification from serving as director of any Egyptian company following conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file Form 59, failure to prepare the Local File or Master File once thresholds are crossed, adopting an unbenchmarked TNMM margin for the Egyptian email-infrastructure entity, or rejecting ETA access to contemporaneous TP documentation during audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA disregards the transaction and imputes an arm's length profit; additional tax is assessed plus a 2% monthly delay surcharge capped at 50% of the additional tax; procedural fine of not less than EGP 5,000 and up to EGP 50,000 for refusal to submit documentation; criminal penalties apply if false statements are certified.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false Transfer Pricing certifications face joint liability for the additional assessment and criminal prosecution for false declaration; after final conviction they may be barred from management positions in Egyptian entities.
